factor.name: Pause > 7 consecutive days
factor.scoring_methodology:
**What this measures**
This factor is a Boolean flag set to true if the protocol has been paused for more than seven consecutive days at least once in the trailing twelve months. It is derived from on-chain pause-event data and updated on each new pause event. A sustained pause -- as distinct from a brief precautionary halt -- indicates either a serious unresolved vulnerability, a governance deadlock preventing the protocol from resuming, or operational instability severe enough to warrant extended downtime.

**Why it matters**
A pause lasting more than seven days is qualitatively different from a brief emergency halt. It signals that the underlying issue was complex enough (or the team's response capacity was insufficient) to prevent rapid resolution. For depositors, a seven-day pause means their capital is locked for a minimum of a week with no certainty of when function resumes. In the dataset, extended pauses have preceded both successful recoveries (e.g., multi-week pauses following white-hat negotiations) and protocol sunsettings (e.g., Raft sunsetted after its exploited state made resumption impossible). Either outcome represents material depositor risk.

**Green / Yellow / Red**
Green: no pause exceeding seven consecutive days in the trailing twelve months. Yellow: one pause between seven and thirty days in the trailing twelve months, with documented resolution and protocol resumption. Red: any pause exceeding thirty consecutive days in the trailing twelve months, or a pause still active at time of assessment.

**Common gray cases**
Planned maintenance pauses announced well in advance (e.g., a scheduled chain migration) may be treated differently from emergency pauses. Curator must verify whether the pause was planned or reactive, and whether user funds were accessible during the pause period.

**Notable historical examples**
No cross-hacked incidents currently linked in database for this factor.

scored_protocols.evidence_summary: V2 has long-running wind-down reserve freezes/caps and deprecated-market restrictions that exceed short emergency-duration thresholds.

scored_protocols.evidence_detail: Independent second review approved yellow-to-red for prolonged reserve freeze duration. This is a V3 incident/continuity score change.
scored_protocols.evidence_summary: Affected Aave V3 WETH/rsETH-related reserves remained frozen long enough after the April 18, 2026 incident to exceed the >7-day pause/freeze threshold before May 10 unfreeze actions.

scored_protocols.evidence_summary: No V4 reserve-freeze duration table was extracted for this pass.

scored_protocols.evidence_detail: The two documented trailing-year pauses were three to four days and roughly twelve hours, both below seven consecutive days.
scored_protocols.evidence_summary: Neither documented trailing-year pause exceeded seven consecutive days: Lens lasted 3-4 days and Solana order flow was restored in roughly 12 hours.

The BTC-staking specification describes timelock, unbonding, slashing, and withdrawal paths rather than an application pause control. Public evidence reviewed does not establish the duration of any protocol pause event, so this factor remains gray.
The retained public Guardian documentation describes an emergency-control pathway but does not provide a complete event-duration record. Whether any pause exceeded seven days is not established.
No retained public pause-event timeline substantiates the v1.7 seven-day pause threshold.

The documented May 2025 EigenPods maintenance pause was expected to last about 16 hours and the protocol announced completion the same day; the reviewed evidence does not establish a pause exceeding seven consecutive days.
Ethena's public governance update says the April 2026 LayerZero OFT bridge pause lasted April 19-20 before restoration. The documented pause was far shorter than seven consecutive days.
The reviewed public sources do not provide the complete pause/unpause event pairs needed to establish maximum consecutive pause duration in the trailing 12 months.
No public report located of a protocol-wide pause exceeding seven consecutive days between 2025-07-24 and 2026-07-24. The reported July 2025 API and order-execution outage lasted minutes, not days.

scored_protocols.evidence_detail: The public deployment record permits program identification but does not itself enumerate pause start/end events or establish that no pause exceeded seven days.
scored_protocols.evidence_summary: Gray: no verified complete on-chain pause-duration dataset was available for the KLend program.
